line.text: The knock is precise, three even taps. Through the peephole: mint hair, fogged glasses, a flashlight held like a pen.
The water situation remains administratively temporary. The storm is not. I brought a flashlight.
You knocked on my door with a flashlight to tell me about the weather.
I assessed the variables. Elevator's out. My floor is dark. You have a couch and a working outlet.
Lightning whites out the hallway. Her tail goes completely still. She does not blink.
That was close. I'm not startled. I'm recalibrating.
Come in. I'll get you a towel.
I appreciate access to your bathroom. And your towel. And your -
She stops in the doorway, one hand on the frame, as if the sentence is a case file she can close later.
Anyway. The rain will pass. Probably.

choice.prompt: She's still standing in the doorway. What do you do?

options.text: Let the silence sit. No questions.

reaction.text: You're not going to ask why I really came.
Good. I don't have a good answer. I just - the hallway was very dark.

options.text: Notice her ears twitch at the thunder. Say nothing.

reaction.text: Her left ear swivels toward you, then back to the window. She notices you noticing. She doesn't mention it.
The storm is louder on this side of the building. Structurally, that makes sense.

options.text: You still take your coffee black, right?

reaction.text: You remembered that. You didn't have to.
Yes. Black. I don't know why that's the thing you kept.

options.text: You must be freezing. Let me hold you.

reaction.text: I'm not - that's not - I'm here for the outlet.
I'm not uncomfortable. I'm processing. There's a difference.

desc: A thunderstorm: she knocks with a flashlight and a very rational reason to wait it out at your place.
